Apple___Apple_scab.description: Causes dark, scabby lesions on leaves and fruit. The fungus overwinters in fallen leaves.
prevention: Rake up and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to remove overwintering spores
Plant scab-resistant apple varieties
Prune to improve air circulation through the canopy
treatment: Apply a fungicide labeled for apple scab starting at bud break
Repeat applications through wet spring weather per label instructions
Remove and destroy visibly infected leaves and fruit

Apple___Black_rot.description: Causes leaf spots, fruit rot, and cankers on branches.
prevention: Prune out dead wood and cankers during dormant season
Remove mummified fruit left on the tree or ground
Maintain overall tree vigor with proper fertilization and watering
treatment: Apply fungicide sprays during the growing season per local guidance
Sanitize pruning tools between cuts to avoid spreading infection

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Bright orange leaf spots; the fungus needs both apple and juniper/cedar trees to complete its life cycle.
prevention: Remove nearby juniper/cedar trees or the galls on them if feasible
Choose rust-resistant apple varieties when planting
treatment: Apply fungicide from pink bud stage through petal fall
Remove heavily infected leaves where practical

Apple___healthy.description: No disease detected — the leaf appears healthy.
prevention: Continue regular watering, fertilization, and pruning
Inspect periodically for early signs of pests or disease

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: White powdery fungal growth on leaves and shoots.
prevention: Prune to improve air circulation
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer
Water at soil level rather than wetting the foliage
treatment: Apply a sulfur-based or potassium bicarbonate fungicide at first sign
Remove and destroy heavily infected shoots

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: No disease detected — the leaf appears healthy.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Rectangular gray-to-tan lesions on leaves, can reduce yield if severe.
prevention: Rotate crops instead of planting corn after corn
Plant resistant hybrids
Till under crop residue to reduce overwintering fungus
treatment: Apply a foliar fungicide if disease appears before tasseling in humid conditions

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Small reddish-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant hybrids
Early planting can help avoid peak rust season
treatment: Usually minor impact; fungicide only needed if infection is severe and early in the season

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Long, cigar-shaped gray-green lesions on leaves.
prevention: Plant resistant hybrids
Rotate crops and manage residue through tillage
treatment: Apply fungicide if disease appears early relative to crop growth stage

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: No disease detected — the leaf appears healthy.
prevention: Continue regular care and periodic inspection

Grape___Black_rot.description: Causes leaf spots and shriveled, mummified fruit.
prevention: Remove mummified berries and infected canes during dormant pruning
Improve canopy airflow through proper training
treatment: Apply fungicide from bud break through veraison, especially in wet weather

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: Tiger-stripe leaf pattern and internal wood decay; a serious trunk disease.
prevention: Avoid pruning during wet weather
Protect large pruning cuts with a wound sealant
treatment: No effective chemical cure exists; remove and destroy severely infected vines/wood

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Brown angular spots on leaves that can merge and cause defoliation.
prevention: Manage canopy for good airflow
Remove infected leaves where practical
treatment: Apply fungicide applications as needed during the growing season

Grape___healthy.description: No disease detected — the leaf appears healthy.
prevention: Continue regular care and periodic inspection

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: Serious bacterial disease spread by the Asian citrus psyllid; causes blotchy mottled leaves and bitter, misshapen fruit.
prevention: Control Asian citrus psyllid populations
Use certified disease-free nursery stock
Remove and destroy infected trees promptly to limit spread
treatment: No cure currently exists; management focuses on prevention and removing infected trees

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Small dark spots on leaves and fruit, can cause leaves to drop.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties
Avoid overhead irrigation
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer
treatment: Copper-based bactericide sprays during dormant season and early growth (limited effect once established)

Remove volunteer potatoes and infected plant debris
Avoid overhead watering
treatment: Apply a fungicide (e.g., chlorothalonil) at first sign, repeating per label

Avoid overhead irrigation, ensure good drainage and airflow
Destroy volunteer plants
treatment: Apply fungicide preventatively during humid weather
Remove and destroy infected plants immediately — it spreads very fast

prevention: Plant resistant varieties
Ensure good plant spacing and airflow
Avoid overhead watering
treatment: Apply sulfur, potassium bicarbonate, or neem oil at first sign

Ensure good airflow between plants

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Small dark, water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed or transplants
Avoid overhead watering
Rotate crops
treatment: Copper-based bactericide (limited effect once established)

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Dark concentric-ring spots, usually starting on older/lower leaves.
prevention: Rotate crops
Mulch to prevent soil splashing onto leaves
Prune lower leaves and stake plants for airflow
treatment: Apply fungicide (chlorothalonil or copper-based) at first sign
Remove infected lower leaves

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Fast-spreading disease causing dark, greasy-looking lesions; can destroy a crop within days in favorable weather.
prevention: Avoid overhead watering, ensure spacing and airflow
Use resistant varieties where available
Avoid handling plants while wet
treatment: Apply fungicide preventatively during cool, wet weather
Remove and destroy infected plants immediately — it spreads very fast

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Yellow spots on upper leaf surface with olive-green mold underneath; common in humid greenhouses.
prevention: Improve greenhouse or garden ventilation
Reduce humidity around plants
Avoid overhead watering
treatment: Apply fungicide, increase airflow, remove infected leaves

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Small circular spots with dark borders and gray centers, starting on lower leaves.
prevention: Rotate crops
Mulch and avoid overhead watering
Remove infected lower leaves early
treatment: Apply fungicide (chlorothalonil or copper-based)
Remove infected plant debris

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Tiny mites causing stippled, yellowing leaves; thrive in hot, dry conditions.
prevention: Avoid drought stress on plants
Maintain humidity around plants
Encourage natural predators like ladybugs and predatory mites
treatment: Apply insecticidal soap or miticide, targeting the undersides of leaves
Repeat treatment as needed

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Brown lesions with concentric rings resembling a target.
prevention: Rotate crops
Avoid overhead watering
Remove crop debris after harvest
treatment: Apply fungicide, remove infected leaves

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Spread by whiteflies; causes upward-curling, yellowing leaves and stunted growth.
prevention: Control whitefly populations
Use resistant varieties where available
Use reflective mulches to deter whiteflies
Remove infected plants promptly
treatment: No cure exists; focus on whitefly control and removing infected plants to limit spread

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Causes mottled light/dark green patterns on leaves and stunted growth.
prevention: Use certified virus-free seed
Disinfect tools and hands between plants
Control aphids, which can spread related viruses
treatment: No cure exists; remove and destroy infected plants, disinfect tools thoroughly
